findings.charge: v9's FX-12 intent names two distinct revocation delivery modes — duplicate AND concurrent — and the corpus collapses them into one entry with the compound value 'duplicate-and-concurrent'. An input corpus whose whole function is enumerating inputs supplies one input for a class that names two deliveries.
evidence: Live v9 FX-12.intent, opening clause: 'Deliver duplicate and concurrent revocations for one generation during cleanup'. The subject carries this text byte-identically in basedOn.pttV9.fx12Intent, so the two modes are named in the artifact's own quotation.

Subject initialStates has exactly one element: id 'FX-12.duplicate-and-concurrent-revocations-during-cleanup', revocations 'duplicate-and-concurrent'. whatIsAuthored reads 'One named duplicate-and-concurrent-revocation case.'

The two modes are separable and behave differently. Duplicate is sequential: v9 R-5 is 'REVOCATION DURING CLEANUP: a second REV arrives for a generation already revoked and mid-cleanup', whose whyDeterministic turns on ordering already fixed — 'exactly one is the linearization point (the first, at r), and later ones are audit facts'. Concurrent is simultaneous arrival, where which revocation becomes 'the first' is decided by the single writer's sequencing rather than by arrival.

v9 has NO race for concurrent revocations. R-5 covers the duplicate case; R-4 is 'CONCURRENT requests for the SAME token', which is concurrent REQUESTS, not revocations. Measured over live v9, the lowercase token 'concurrent' occurs exactly once in the entire artifact — in FX-12's intent. This corpus is therefore the only place the concurrent-revocation delivery is pinned anywhere, and it does not pin it as a distinct input.
permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2, same cycle and same author, gives one initialState per named position — four positions, four entries — rather than one compound entry.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: A fixture author building to this corpus satisfies it with a single sequential duplicate-REV delivery. Nothing in the corpus distinguishes that from a run that also delivers two revocations concurrently, so the concurrent half of FX-12's named delivery can be skipped and the corpus will still read as covered. Because v9 supplies no race semantics for concurrent revocations, no downstream artifact catches the gap either — the corpus is the last line.
refutationAttempted: Read 'duplicate and concurrent' as one compound delivery rather than two. Even on that reading the corpus must say what the single delivery is, and 'duplicate-and-concurrent' is not a delivery — it is the conjunction of two, left unresolved. The corpus does not state whether one delivery exhibits both properties or whether two deliveries are required.

Argue that enumerating deliveries is the fixture author's job, not the corpus's. That is refuted inside this cycle: fx5 v2 enumerates four separate initialStates for FX-5's four named positions rather than one 'four-positions' entry, and it was revised to that shape in response to review.
findings.whatWouldLandIt: Split into two named initialStates — a duplicate delivery (a second REV for an already-revoked generation mid-cleanup) and a concurrent delivery (revocations arriving simultaneously for one generation mid-cleanup) — keeping journalBytes and cleanupBound NOT-AUTHORED in each.

findings.at: initialStates[0]; absence of an assertsNamedNotAuthored field
findings.charge: Two of the five asserts v9's FX-12 intent names are absent from the corpus, and neither omission is excused by the NOT-AUTHORED markers. The two dropped asserts are the record-level half of the idempotence property and the behavioural half of the bound property — between them, one half of each thing FX-12 is stated to prove.
evidence: v9 FX-12.intent names five asserts: (1) one linearization point; (2) all attempts journaled; (3) cleanup neither restarted nor extended; (4) CLN written exactly once; (5) the declared bound honored with bound-exhaustion journaled as a residual rather than retried.

Mapped against the corpus: (1) carried as oneLinearizationPoint true; (3) carried as cleanupRestartedOrExtended false; (4) carried as clnWrittenExactlyOnce true. (2) ABSENT. (5) ABSENT — cleanupBound NOT-AUTHORED carries the number, not the residual-versus-retry behaviour.

v9 FX-12.proves: 'ENFORCEMENT (of the state-level idempotence and the bound)'. Assert (2) is the record-level half of that idempotence, made express at v9 R-5.whyDeterministic: 'Revocation is idempotent at the state level and non-idempotent at the record level -- every revocation attempt is journaled, exactly one is the linearization point (the first, at r), and later ones are audit facts.' The corpus keeps the state-level half and drops the record-level half.

Assert (5) is a behavioural choice, not a number, and v9 states it independently of any number at R-6: 'exhausting it journals a residual rather than looping.' The dispatch forbids authoring 'a cleanup-bound number'; it does not forbid naming residual-versus-retry.

The NOT-AUTHORED defence fails on the artifact's own precedent: clnWrittenExactlyOnce is itself a record-cardinality assertion stated while journalBytes is NOT-AUTHORED. The artifact therefore demonstrably can state a record-cardinality property without authoring bytes, and states one while omitting the other of the same shape.

It fails again on the cycle's precedent: permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2 carries journalBytes NOT-AUTHORED and cleanupBoundNumber NOT-AUTHORED AND a separate assertsNamedNotAuthored list of all three v9 FX-5 asserts, at top level and in every entry. The subject has no such field. permission-fx11-input-corpus.v1 likewise carries its class's asserts as explicit fields.
The omission is visible against text the artifact itself quotes: basedOn.pttV9.fx12Intent reproduces all five asserts verbatim.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: FX-12's whole subject is that revocation is idempotent at the state level and non-idempotent at the record level. A fixture built to this corpus asserts one linearization point and one CLN, and need never assert that the duplicate revocation produced its own journal record — a host that silently swallows the second revocation passes. Likewise, with residual-versus-retry unnamed, a host that retries on bound exhaustion instead of journaling a residual passes. Those are the two failure modes 'ENFORCEMENT of the state-level idempotence AND the bound' exists to catch.
refutationAttempted: Argue journalBytes NOT-AUTHORED already carries assert (2). It carries bytes; assert (2) is a completeness property over however many records exist. fx5 v2 settles the distinction inside this cycle by carrying both kinds in separate fields.

Argue an input corpus states inputs, not asserts, so omitting asserts is in scope. The subject does not follow that rule — three of the five asserts are stated as fields of initialStates[0], and oneLinearizationPoint, clnWrittenExactlyOnce and cleanupRestartedOrExtended are post-conditions, not initial state. Having chosen to carry asserts, the corpus carries an incomplete set.
findings.whatWouldLandIt: Add an assertsNamedNotAuthored field in the fx5 v2 shape, listing all five v9 FX-12 asserts verbatim — including 'all attempts journaled' and 'the declared bound honored with bound-exhaustion journaled as a residual rather than retried' — at top level and inside each initialState, with journalBytes and cleanupBound left NOT-AUTHORED.

notCharged: The artifact contains no explicit 'Does not claim QUALIFIED' line, unlike several siblings. Nothing in it claims QUALIFIED, so the attack fails on the facts and this is an absent belt-and-braces line rather than a defect.

initialStates carries post-conditions (oneLinearizationPoint, clnWrittenExactlyOnce, cleanupRestartedOrExtended) under a key named for initial state. This is a naming imprecision shared with sibling corpora in the same cycle and is subsumed by B2's remedy; it is not charged separately.

verdictStatement: REJECT at 2 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean — all three cited digests match, the fx12Intent quotation is byte-identical to live v9, the subject did not move, required-now is unmoved, OBL-FX-AUTHORING is explicitly not closed, and no journal bytes, CLN bytes or bound number are authored anywhere. The artifact fails on coverage of the class it names. v9's FX-12 intent names two revocation delivery modes and five asserts; this corpus supplies one compound entry and three asserts. The concurrent-revocation delivery is pinned nowhere else in v9 — the lowercase token 'concurrent' occurs exactly once in the whole contract, in FX-12's own intent — so a corpus that folds it into a compound label leaves it unpinned everywhere. And the two dropped asserts are precisely the record-level half of the idempotence and the behavioural half of the bound, which together are what FX-12 is stated to prove. Neither omission is excused by NOT-AUTHORED: the artifact states clnWrittenExactlyOnce while journalBytes is NOT-AUTHORED, proving it can state record-cardinality without bytes, and permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2 in this same cycle carries NOT-AUTHORED bytes and a separate assertsNamedNotAuthored list of every v9 assert — a field this artifact does not have.
